direction_note: Cycle 8: scrapped jpy_fiscal_year_end_repatriation with its lesson (fiscal-calendar JPY flows leave no spot footprint in Tokyo hours; controls beat the fiscal months; April check positives were 2021-23 drift). Registered, revised with the Critic (eight revisions: Friday exit at the 20:00 UTC bar, Monday-only entry decision with a causal fallback exit, start 2013, quarter-paired control test, FOMC attribution, replication on the difference with a 14-day Japan shift, honest power, two-grid spec), built, fixed once at code review (fallback window ended at the next entered week's entry so 2013 data gaps could not hold a position for weeks), approved, and tested index_earnings_season_premium (long the Nasdaq 100 CFD Monday 15:00 UTC to Friday 20:00 UTC in reporting weeks vs every other week). Verdict kill:stage_a and below every pre-registered threshold: best season cell (start_off 17, 5 weeks, stop 2 x ATR20) design +0.062 R (t 0.83, 96 trades), check +0.066 R (t 1.03, 120); matching control design -0.039 R (154), check +0.026 R (189); quarter-paired season-minus-control D design +0.109 R (t 0.92 over 20 quarters), check +0.037 R (t 0.49); ex-FOMC weeks design +0.133 R, check +0.006 R, so the check-period excess sat in FOMC weeks; ex-2013 design +0.078 R (t 0.58); every start_off 10 season cell lost in design (-0.014 to -0.077 R), so the family is not consistently positive; spread 0.8 percent of the stop, financing -0.02 R per trade, fallback exits 7 of 96 season and 24 of 154 control weeks. Lesson for the next Director to record: a weekly-hold reporting-season excess on index CFDs is small, inconsistent across the window family, partly FOMC, and under t 1 everywhere; do not retry with daily holds (cost-dead in the design years), other window offsets, the S&P as primary, or option-expiry overlaps. Programme status: 33 scrap, 4 rejected, 0 holdout touches, every price/quote/clock dimension including month-of-year and the reporting calendar now measured. Direction change: parallel sessions have wired external inputs into the engine today (data/external: calendar.parquet with surprise_z, cot.parquet, vol.parquet, tfx.parquet, tfx_daily.parquet; ext_series in hypotheses; F.ext_asof and related accessors; leak tests cover them), so the loop should continue with hypotheses that condition on those inputs rather than stop: candidates are scheduled-release surprise continuation gated by surprise_z and the release's own clock, CFTC leveraged-fund positioning extremes as a state for the existing USDJPY flows, implied-vol (VXN, EVZ, VIX) gating of the box and gotobi legs, and the TFX daily open-interest change as a retail dip-buying proxy for USDJPY and AUDJPY; the Critic will reject any price-only re-slice.

judgments.lesson: Japanese fiscal-calendar flows do not show up as a tradeable spot flow in Tokyo hours net of costs, and the month-of-year dimension is now measured. Pre-registered per-leg rule 1 failed for both legs on all 24 stage A cells (USDJPY, design 2010-2017, check 2018-2023, Tokyo session 00:00-06:00 UTC, stop 0.25 or 0.5 x ATR20, median stop 21.4 pips, fill spread 0.63 pips). ye_short (last 5 or 10 weekdays of March, or March and September): every March-only cell lost in design (-0.022 to -0.093 R, t -0.27 to -1.23, 40-80 trades); the best hypothesis cell by design t (March+September, 5 days, sl 0.25) made +0.026 R (t 0.25, month-window-clustered t 0.21, -0.034 R without its best month-window, +0.022 R without gotobi dates) and -0.047 R in check; the ordinary-month controls (same windows in months 1, 2, 5, 7, 8, 11) did better in design (+0.025 to +0.060 R) and in check (+0.035 to +0.155 R, t up to 2.6), so the fiscal excess is negative and the Tokyo-session short in the last weekdays of any month is a generic, cost-level month-end pattern already covered by the atlas's month-ordinal day types and the patterns_usdjpy fix-short. ny_long (first 5 or 10 weekdays of April, or April and October): every cell lost in design (-0.083 to -0.111 R, t -0.49 to -1.88) while check was positive (+0.04 to +0.13 R) against negative controls (-0.02 to -0.08 R), which is the 2021-2023 USDJPY rally drift the Critic predicted, not a new-fiscal-year flow. Stage B/C on the ye_short arm: pooled check -0.034 R (180 trades), walk-forward -0.025 R (340), negative at 1.5x costs, 3 of 3 markets positive in design only by cells with t below 0.7. Do not retry with other day counts, the London session or a full-day hold, the fix minute, September or October alone, the Japanese half-year dividend repatriation (June/December), an AUD or EUR fiscal year-end, or a JPY cross as primary; if repatriation exists it is hedged forward or executed off the Tokyo clock and leaves no spot footprint this programme can trade.
judgments.notes: Killed at the pipeline (G2 check, G2b walk-forward, G4 1.5x costs) and at the Director's per-leg rule 1 read from the trials table. hypotheses.title: Aggregate earnings-announcement premium: hold the Nasdaq 100 CFD long Monday-to-Friday only in the weeks when most S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 companies report (weeks 2 to 6 after each quarter-end), with every other week of the year as the control arm; replication on the S&P 500 and Nikkei 225 CFDs
hypotheses.rationale: Mechanism: a risk premium, not a flow. Savor and Wilson (2016, Journal of Finance, 'Earnings announcements and systematic risk') show that firm earnings news is systematic information, that the aggregate market earns a markedly higher average return on days when many firms announce than on other days (on the order of 10 basis points a day against a few basis points on quiet days), and that this is compensation for bearing concentrated cash-flow and discount-rate news; Barber, De George, Lehavy and Trueman (2013) find the announcement premium in most developed markets, including Japan. The participants are investors who cut exposure or buy protection into the reporting season and are paid, on average, for holding through it; the other side is whoever supplies that exposure. Reporting is concentrated by the calendar: large US companies report from about the second week after a quarter-end for four to five weeks (mid-January to mid-February, mid-April to mid-May, mid-July to mid-August, mid-October to mid-November), and Japanese companies report in overlapping windows about ten days later. The programme has never tested a risk premium on indices: the index work tested calendar flows (turn-of-month, option expiry, pension rebalancing), overnight drift, pre-holiday drift, intraday momentum, FOMC drift, dip-buying and vol timing, none of which is the announcement premium, and the charter's warning that long-only index tests pass by luck 2-8 percent of the time is met with a same-year control arm (every non-season week) that cancels the index drift. Design: H1 bars on the Nasdaq 100 CFD (USATECHIDXUSD, usable from 2012; 2011 has six days of data), one trade per week: long at the first bar at or after Monday 14:30 UTC, time exit at the first bar at or after Friday 20:30 UTC, stop 1.0 or 2.0 x ATR20, no target. Season weeks are defined from the calendar before any data is seen: a week is a season week when its Monday falls start_off to start_off + 7 x n_weeks - 1 days after the first day of the quarter (start_off 10 or 17; n_weeks 4 or 5), so the four cells bracket the reporting calendar without reading it from the data; the control arm is every other Monday of the year. Counts (USATECHIDXUSD design 2012-2017, from the calendar and the bar census, no outcomes): about 96-120 season weeks and 190-215 control weeks per cell before holiday and missing-bar skips (about 45-52 Mondays a year have a 14:xx UTC bar), check 2018-2023 similar; JP225 is usable from 2014 and USA500 from 2012. Costs (engine index costs: raw spread, 1 point of slippage per fill, financing per night): the Nasdaq CFD spread was about 2-3 points on a 2,500-4,000 index in 2012-2014, so a weekly round trip costs about 0.15-0.25 percent of the index including four nights of financing; a 1.0 x ATR20 stop is about 1.5-2 percent of the index, so the cost is about 0.10-0.13 R at sl 1.0 and 0.05-0.07 R at sl 2.0, falling in later years as the spread narrowed. Expected: if heavy reporting weeks earn about +0.4 to +0.5 percent against about +0.1 percent for other weeks, the season arm nets about +0.12 R at sl 1.0 with sd about 1 R, design t about 1.2-1.4 on about 100 trades, and the control arm sits near zero or slightly negative after costs; P(design t >= 2 | effect real at that size) is about 25-30 percent, so a kill is weak evidence and a pass is strong evidence. The most likely failure is that the premium is concentrated on the announcement days themselves rather than spread over the week, so a five-day hold dilutes it below the weekly cost, or that it is a pre-2010 result that has been arbitraged. Human execution: one order a week for about 18 weeks a year, placed Monday morning New York time with a Friday afternoon exit; executable on a prop account that allows index CFDs, and its risk sits in a different instrument and week structure from the USDJPY basket.
hypotheses.rules:
All times UTC. Bars: H1, sparse (whole hours are missing in 2012-2013 and 2015-2017); locate every time by timestamp with F.first_bar_at_or_after and never assume one bar per hour.

WEEK SELECTION (calendar, UTC): mondays = unique F.utc_dates(m) with F.weekday(d) == 0 and d >= start. For each Monday d: months = d.astype('datetime64[M]'); mi = months.astype(int) % 12 (0 = January); qstart = (months - (mi % 3) months).astype('datetime64[D]') = the first day of the calendar quarter containing d; off = (d - qstart) in days (0..91). season(d) = start_off <= off < start_off + 7 * n_weeks. Arm p['arm'] = 'season' selects Mondays with season(d) true; p['arm'] = 'ctrl' selects Mondays with season(d) false (every other week of the year). Raise on an unknown arm value. US and Japanese holidays are not excluded (no calendar in the engine); a holiday Monday without a bar near the entry time is skipped by the delay guard.

ENTRY: (eh, em) = F.parse_hhmm(p['entry_utc']) = 14:30; ei = F.first_bar_at_or_after(m, d, eh, em). Skip the week if ei < 1, or ei >= m.n, or m.ts[ei] is more than max_delay_min (90) minutes after d 14:30 UTC. sig = ei - 1, so the fill is at the open of bar ei (ask side plus slippage). entry_long[sig] = True; entry_type[sig] = 0; valid_bars[sig] = 1. Long only; the control arm is also long (it measures the drift and cost that the season arm must beat).

STOP: daily = F.daily_bars(m); ATR20 = daily.to_bars(F.atr_prev(daily, atr_n = 20)), known at the start of the trading day. Read ATR20 at ei, not sig. Skip the week if ATR20[ei] is not finite or <= 0. sl_dist[sig] = sl_atr x ATR20[ei] (price units, > 0). tp_dist = NaN (no target). max_bars = 0.

EXIT: f = d + 4 days (the Friday of the same week); (xh, xm) = F.parse_hhmm(p['exit_utc']) = 20:30; xi = F.first_bar_at_or_after(m, f, xh, xm). Skip the week if xi >= m.n, or xi <= ei, or m.ts[xi] is more than max_exit_delay_min (180) minutes after f 20:30 UTC (a missing Friday close must not stretch the hold into the next week). exit_long[xi - 1] = True, so the position closes at the open of the first bar at or after Friday 20:30 UTC. No other exits, no filters, one trade per selected week; the executor blocks overlapping entries.

PARAMETERS (every one read from p): arm (grid 'season', 'ctrl'), start_off (grid 10, 17), n_weeks (grid 4, 5), sl_atr (grid 1.0, 2.0); fixed entry_utc '14:30', exit_utc '20:30', max_delay_min 90, max_exit_delay_min 180, atr_n 20, start '2012-01-01'. Module GRID = the full 16 cells so the checker exercises every value. Spec grids: stage A on USATECHIDXUSD runs all 16 cells (the 'ctrl' cells are control arms and run only there); stages B, C, the walk-forward and any holdout run the season arm only, arm 'season' x start_off x n_weeks x sl_atr (8 cells).

EXPECTED COUNTS (USATECHIDXUSD design 2012-2017, a check for the Builder and the checker): season weeks about 85-110 per cell after skips (96 calendar weeks at n_weeks 4, 120 at n_weeks 5, less about 10 percent for holiday Mondays and missing bars), control weeks about 170-200; check 2018-2023 similar. A count far from these means the week selection is wrong.

REPORTING (stage A table and stage C, computed from the trades; all 16 stage A rows read from the trials table, stage 'A'): per cell the number of trades, avg R, trade-level t, season-window-clustered t (R averaged per calendar quarter of the entry date, then t over those quarter means), mean fill spread in index points and as a share of the stop, mean financing per trade in R, by-year avg R, for design and for check; for the chosen cell the avg R by quarter-month (January, April, July, October seasons), the avg R without the best ceil(W/8) design season windows (W = the cell's number of design quarter-windows, about 24, so 3 dropped), and a per-year table of chosen minus matching-control avg R in design and check.

pre_registered.kill_if: (1) Hypothesis-cell floor on USATECHIDXUSD, applied by the Director from all 16 stage A rows in the trials table (stage 'A') even if the pipeline reports a candidate (the automatic stage A gate ranks all 16 cells by design t, so a control cell can clear it): among the 8 season cells with at least 60 design trades, the chosen cell is the one with the highest trade-level design t (the pipeline's own ranking); it must have design avg R > 0, trade-level t >= 1 and season-window-clustered t >= 1 (R averaged per calendar quarter of the entry date, then t over those quarter means); otherwise scrap. If the automatic floor is cleared only by a ctrl cell, the B/C output is ignored and the hypothesis is scrapped under this rule. (2) Control difference: at the chosen cell, design avg R(chosen) minus design avg R(the ctrl cell with the same start_off, n_weeks and sl_atr) must be >= +0.06 R, and check avg R(chosen) minus check avg R(matching ctrl) must be > 0 (the stage A backtests span design and check). The control is long in every other week, so it carries the index drift and the same costs; a season result the control matches is drift, not a premium, and the hypothesis dies with the lesson that long-only index holds in 2012-2023 earn the drift in every week alike. If promoted, the locked holdout run also runs the matching ctrl cell (same touch, counted), and a holdout where chosen minus ctrl <= 0 is a fail even if the raw holdout avg R > 0. (3) Breadth across seasons: at the chosen cell, at least 3 of the 4 quarter seasons (January, April, July, October reporting windows) must be positive in design, and design avg R must stay > 0 after dropping the best ceil(W/8) design quarter-windows (W about 24, so 3 dropped); a premium carried by one reporting month or by two or three quarters is an episode, not a premium. (4) Regime: at least 3 of the 6 design years positive at the chosen cell. (5) Costs: the hard gate (positive at 1.5x costs) stands; the mean fill spread as a share of the stop and the financing per trade are reported; if the chosen cell is positive gross but negative net, the lesson is that the premium exists but is smaller than a weekly CFD round trip, about 0.15-0.25 percent of the index. (6) Replication: at the chosen cell read from the stage B trials table on each market, the design avg R pooled date-clustered over USA500IDXUSD and JPNIDXJPY (average the same-week R across the two, then t over weeks) must be > 0, and the pooled-check hard gate (avg R > 0 with >= 30 trades) and the walk-forward gate stand; a Nasdaq-only result with the S&P 500 negative is scrapped as noise, because the two indices share the reporting calendar and most of their constituents' news. (7) Pass bar: a positive result below the programme bar (design t >= 2 at the chosen cell with the design and check control differences positive) is recorded as below the bar and is not promoted. Honest expectation: about +0.12 R net at sl 1.0 on about 100 design season weeks (cost about 0.10-0.13 R at sl 1.0, 0.05-0.07 R at sl 2.0; a net +0.12 R needs about +0.45 percent per season week gross), design t 1.2-1.4; P(design t >= 2 | effect real at that size) about 25-30 percent, so a kill is weak evidence and a pass is strong evidence; the most likely failure is that the premium sits on the announcement days only and a five-day hold dilutes it below the weekly cost, or that it was arbitraged before 2012.

hypotheses.why_different: Every prior index test measured a flow or a drift: calendar flows at month-end, option expiry and pension rebalancing (index_flows: turn-of-month when stocks beat bonds was the best near miss), the overnight and European-open drift (dead on cost), pre-holiday drift (below the bar), first-half-hour to last-half-hour momentum (cost-dead), pre-FOMC drift (since 2016 only), dip-buying (index drift in disguise) and vol-managed exposure (safety, not edge). None conditioned on the corporate reporting calendar, and none tested a risk premium with a same-year control: here the control arm is long in every non-season week of the same years, so the index drift, the costs and the financing are identical in both arms and only the reporting-week excess is scored. The window is fixed from the calendar (days after quarter-end) before any data is seen, bracketed by four cells rather than read from the data, and the mechanism names a published, out-of-sample-replicated premium (Savor and Wilson 2016; Barber, De George, Lehavy and Trueman 2013) with a reason for it (systematic information risk) rather than a seasonal pattern. It is the index-side analogue of the one unscanned calendar dimension, and the replication on the S&P 500 and the Nikkei 225 tests the mechanism rather than the Nasdaq's own history.

director.direction_note: Cycle 8 scraps the fiscal-year-end repatriation test with the lesson that Japanese fiscal-calendar flows leave no tradeable spot footprint in Tokyo hours (every March-only and April/October cell lost in design; the ordinary-month controls did better; the April check positives were the 2021-2023 USDJPY drift), which closes the month-of-year dimension for FX. One hypothesis is registered on the index side, where the programme has only ever tested flows and drifts: the aggregate earnings-announcement premium (Savor and Wilson 2016), long the Nasdaq 100 CFD Monday-to-Friday in the reporting weeks (start 10 or 17 days after quarter-end, 4 or 5 weeks) against a control arm that is long in every other week of the same years, so the long-only-on-a-rising-index objection is answered inside the design; stops 1 or 2 x ATR20; 16 cells at stage A on USATECHIDXUSD (usable from 2012), season arm only in B/C with replication on USA500IDXUSD and JPNIDXJPY; about 100 design season weeks, expected +0.12 R and t 1.2-1.4, about 25-30 percent likely to reach the pass bar if real. After the review step the Director must again set specs/auto/index_earnings_season_premium.json so that stage_a carries the full 16-cell grid and the spec grid holds arm = season only, and must read all 16 stage A rows from the trials table (stats_json is nested design/check/all). Programme status for the user, unchanged from cycle 7 and now stronger: this is the last mechanism of a different kind that the Director can name from price, quote and clock data alone; if it is negative, the loop should be stopped until external data is added (scheduled-event calendar with surprise sizes, retail positioning, options risk reversals and implied vol, FX swap basis) or the work is redirected to the sizing and risk design of the existing USDJPY basket.

reasons: Worth one run once fixed. It is not a duplicate. No earlier test conditions index holds on the reporting calendar. prior_index_flows tested option expiry, pension rebalancing and turn-of-month. prior_flow_atlas scanned intraday clock windows by day type, not multi-day week-of-quarter holds, so its t >= 3.7 Bonferroni bar does not strictly apply and the programme bar (design t >= 2) does. The same-year control arm (long in every non-season week on the same instrument, with the same costs and financing) is the right defence against the charter's warning about long-only index tests. Grid: 8 hypothesis cells and 8 controls, all fixed from the calendar.

BLOCKER, the exit as written does not exist for most of the year. The H1 bar census (timestamps only, 2012-2023, no outcomes) shows that the Dukascopy US100, US500 and JP225 CFDs stop at 21:00 UTC on Fridays during US daylight saving time. The last Friday bar is therefore stamped 20:00. first_bar_at_or_after(Friday 20:30) returns the Sunday reopen, which fails the 180-minute guard. On USATECHIDXUSD the exit bar is found on 0 of 29-31 daylight-saving Fridays in every year from 2012 to 2023, against nearly all winter Fridays. As written, the April and July seasons and nearly all of October disappear. The season arm would keep about 5 weeks a year, below the 60-trade minimum, and kill rule 3 (3 of 4 seasons positive) could not be scored. With exit_utc 19:30 the exit bar (20:00 UTC) is found on 565 of 609 Fridays.

Contract violation, the entry depends on bars four days ahead. 'Skip the week if xi >= m.n, or m.ts[xi] is more than 180 minutes late' makes Monday's entry signal depend on whether Friday bars exist and when they are stamped. That is information that is not available at the close of the signal bar, and it is exactly what silently deletes the daylight-saving weeks. On the US100 dev horizon the stage-0 truncation probes happen to land in control weeks (2019-01-10 and 2023-01-03), so the automated test may not catch it with the season default. A probe inside any selected week would flag it, and a leak is an immediate scrap. The carry_cross_weekend_premium Builder hit the same problem and had to deviate from the spec.

The mechanism's support is overstated. Savor and Wilson (2016) and Barber, De George, Lehavy and Trueman (2013) document a firm-level premium of announcers over non-announcers. Abnormal returns sum to roughly zero across a cap-weighted index, so that spread does not carry over to a long index position by construction. The figure of about 10 bp a day against a few bp matches Savor and Wilson (2013) on macro-announcement days (CPI, employment, FOMC: about 11 bp against about 1 bp), not earnings seasons. The index trade needs a separate claim, that the market itself earns more in heavy reporting weeks. The evidence for that is older and shaped differently: Penman (1987) found aggregate returns concentrated early in the first month of each quarter, partly in days 0-9, which these cells put in the control arm. Index variance also does not rise much in reporting season (single-stock volatility rises, implied correlation falls), which weakens a systematic-risk story at the index level.

The expected size is implausible and the test has little power. The pre-registered gross excess is about +0.35% per season week, or about 6% a year from 18 weeks; an effect that large would not have survived publication. A realistic excess is 0 to +0.1% a week, 0 to +0.08 R at sl 1.0. The sample: about 85 season weeks against about 165 control weeks, with R sd about 1.1 at sl 1.0, gives a standard error of the difference of about 0.14 R. So a realistic effect cannot be resolved, and a kill is weak evidence.

Kill rules 1, 3, 4 and 6 mostly measure index drift and stop width. Only rule 2 is drift-neutral, and its +0.06 R threshold is less than half a standard error. If the true difference is zero, P(design difference >= +0.06) is about 0.33 and P(check difference > 0) is 0.5. The programme has already measured how noisy calendar subsets of Nasdaq weeks are. In index_flows, the opex-week long (O1) made +0.173 R (design t 1.75) against -0.019 R for non-opex weeks (C1, 207 weeks), then +0.044 against +0.067 R in check.

Confound with FOMC. In every cell the season windows contain all four first-month-of-quarter FOMC meetings (late January, late April or early May, late July, late October or early November) and the US advance GDP releases. The control holds the other four meetings across about 33 weeks. About 20-22% of season weeks contain an FOMC decision, against about 12% of control weeks. prior_fomc_cycle found a pre-FOMC drift (before costs) only since 2016, which is the check period where rule 2 needs a positive difference. A positive season-minus-control result could be that already-measured drift rather than an earnings premium.

Replication rule 6 scores the raw season avg R, and index drift can pass it. Weekly S&P 500 returns track the Nasdaq 100 closely (correlation about 0.9), so the S&P is more a plumbing check than an independent replication. JP225 is barely usable before 2014: Monday entries 0/46 in 2012 and 27/45 in 2013; Friday exits (at 19:30) 2/47 in 2012, 23/47 in 2013 and 26/51 in 2017. That leaves about 60-70 design season weeks. Japanese companies with a March year-end report about two weeks after US large caps, so the US windows test spill-over from the US season on JP225, not the local premium.

Costs: medium. US100 census for 2013-2017: ATR20 is 0.8-1.25% of price; the Monday 15:00 spread is about 2 points in 2013-2014 and about 1 point in 2015-2017; slippage is 1 point per fill. The engine charges financing at the quote rate plus 2.5% a year on 6 night-weights for a Monday-Friday hold, because it triples Wednesday, not the 4 nights assumed. That puts the cost at about 0.1-0.2 R at sl 1.0 and 0.05-0.1 R at sl 2.0. The cost is the same in both arms, so the difference test is not affected by it, but the tradeable season arm needs an excess at least as large as the cost. Bars from 2012 carry no spread at all: bid equals ask on 100% of US100 and 87% of US500 H1 bars in 2012 (about 8% in 2013). So 2012 trades are under-costed and unaffected by the 1.5x cost stress.

Spec plumbing. apply_review writes spec.grid = the hypothesis grid (all 16 cells) and stage_a = {market} with no stage A grid. Unless the spec is edited, stage B and the walk-forward would rank and choose among the control cells too, which contradicts the stated plan (stage A: 16 cells; B, C, walk-forward and holdout: the 8 season cells).
reviews.revisions:
1) Exit time: change exit_utc to '19:30' and measure the 180-minute guard from 19:30. The fill is at the open of the 20:00 UTC bar, which is 16:00 New York during daylight saving and 15:00 in winter. State the real fill times in the rules: entry at the open of the 15:00 UTC bar (H1 bars are stamped at the open), exit at the open of the 20:00 UTC bar.
2) Decide the entry from Monday information only: ei found, the bar no more than 90 minutes after Monday 14:30, ATR20 finite and > 0, date >= start, and the arm's week selection. Delete every skip that depends on the Friday bar. Exit plumbing: (a) normal exit: xi = first bar at or after Friday exit_utc; if xi < m.n, xi > ei and m.ts[xi] is no more than max_exit_delay_min late, set exit_long[xi - 1] = True. (b) Fallback: set exit_long[j] = True on every bar j of that week with ts in [Friday 20:00 UTC, following Monday 12:00 UTC). A week whose Friday session is missing or cut short then exits at the first bar after the gap instead of running into the next trade week. Report the number of fallback (non-Friday) exits in each arm.
3) Set start to '2013-01-01' (2012 index bars have no spread in the data; 2011 has six days). Expected design (2013-2017) counts: about 70-90 season weeks per cell and about 140-170 control weeks.
4) Replace kill rule 2 with a quarter-paired test. For the chosen cell and its matching ctrl cell (same start_off, n_weeks and sl_atr), compute D_q = mean R of the season weeks in calendar quarter q minus mean R of the non-season weeks in the same quarter, using quarters with at least one week in each arm. Require mean D > 0 with t(D over quarters) >= 1.0 in design, and mean D > 0 in check. This threshold matches the pre-registered +0.12 R against about 0 R. Rule 7 (promotion) requires revised rule 2. The holdout keeps the pre-registered 'chosen minus matching ctrl > 0'.
5) FOMC attribution: report D in design and in check after dropping, from both arms, every week that contains a scheduled FOMC decision. Take the dates from the 'Federal Funds Rate' rows in data/external/calendar_spoluan/forex_factory_calendar_YYYY.csv. Those rows are stamped about 8 hours ahead of UTC: the row '2014-01-30 03:00' is the 29 January 2014 decision. If the design D excluding FOMC weeks is <= 0, scrap with the lesson that the season excess is the pre-FOMC drift already measured in prior_fomc_cycle.
6) Score replication on the difference, not on raw season R. Run the matching ctrl cell of the chosen season cell once each on USA500IDXUSD and JPNIDXJPY (counted trials, design and check only, horizon cut at the holdout start, for example scripts/run_backtest.py with --end 2024-01-01). Rule 6 then requires the pooled date-clustered season-minus-ctrl difference over the two markets to be > 0 in design; the pooled-check and walk-forward hard gates stand as written. For JP225, add a fixed parameter jp_shift_days = 14, not in the grid, added to start_off when m.sym starts with 'JPN', because Tokyo companies with a March year-end report about two weeks after US large caps. If the Director declines that change, rule 6 must state that the JP225 run measures spill-over from the US season. JP225 is usable from 2014, about 60-70 design season weeks.
7) Restate the rationale and expectations. reviews.notes_for_builder: Times: H1 bars are stamped at the bar open. For Monday, F.first_bar_at_or_after(m, mondays, 14, 30) returns the 15:00 UTC bar: ei is that bar, sig = ei - 1 is the 14:00 bar, and the fill is at 15:00 UTC. For Friday, with exit_utc '19:30', xi is the 20:00 UTC bar and exit_long[xi - 1] (the 19:00 bar) closes the trade at the 20:00 open; that bar exists on 565 of 609 Fridays from 2012 to 2023 on USATECHIDXUSD. Do NOT skip a week because the Friday exit bar is missing or late. The entry may use only Monday information (follow the pattern in strategies/auto/carry_cross_weekend_premium.py). Place the normal exit marker when the exit bar is found, and also set exit_long on every bar of that week with ts in [Friday 20:00 UTC, following Monday 12:00 UTC) as a causal fallback; markers on bars with no open position are ignored by the executor. Week selection: mondays = unique UTC dates with F.weekday == 0 and date >= start. Quarter start: months = d.astype('datetime64[M]'); q0 = (months - (months.astype(np.int64) % 12 % 3).astype('timedelta64[M]')).astype('datetime64[D]'); off = (d - q0).astype(int). Unit-check before running: 2015-02-16 gives q0 2015-01-01 and off 46; 2015-04-13 gives off 12. season = start_off <= off < start_off + 7 * n_weeks. arm 'season' keeps season Mondays, arm 'ctrl' keeps the others; raise ValueError on any other value. If jp_shift_days is adopted, add it to start_off only when m.sym starts with 'JPN' (default 14, not in the grid; it has no effect on the primary market, so the grid-sensitivity check will not test it). Holiday Mondays (MLK Day, Presidents' Day) do have a 15:00 UTC CFD bar in the data, so they are traded; that is expected. Stop: ATR20 from F.atr_prev(F.daily_bars(m), p['atr_n']) via to_bars, read at ei; skip only if it is not finite or <= 0. sl_dist[sig] = p['sl_atr'] * ATR20[ei]; entry_type 0, valid_bars 1, tp_dist NaN, max_bars 0. Read every key from p: arm, start_off, n_weeks, sl_atr, entry_utc, exit_utc, max_delay_min, max_exit_delay_min, atr_n, start (plus jp_shift_days). The module GRID keeps the 16 cells so the checker exercises arm. Expected counts for the checker on design years with start 2013: about 80 (n_weeks 4) or 100 (n_weeks 5) calendar season weeks before the few skips; a count far below that means the week selection or the Friday exit is wrong. For the Director's reporting: compute the quarter-paired difference D and the FOMC-excluded D from the trade lists of the chosen and matching ctrl cells.
